doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
doc.interviewee: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams

chapter: Cage on songs, cane work, records and family
title: Cutting sugar cane near Smithfield and Napoleonville
summary: Cage says he was a poor cane cutter who would sometimes sing; he worked at Smithfield across the river from Baton Rouge and at Napoleonville, and kept ahead of the cutters behind him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: That must be from Slavery Time. It is. You must know plenty of songs from Slavery Time. Oh I do, that's all I know. Did you ever cut any cane?

Oh yes, I was a pretty good butcher for cane. I'd ruin more than I cut. You'd ruin more than you cut? I ain't been on a cane before I've been in pain. Cut it too short, you know. Too long and leaves. I used to go ever, you know. I used to go ever fall. Low top and high bottom, huh? Yes, when I cut it low bottom, top.
That's what I mean. Low top and high bottom when you cut it. Did you sing when you cut cane?
Sometimes I sang. Sometimes I wasn't just going. I'd be raising more or less trying to keep up. You know, if you get behind, I'd have to put a band on you. The boys and I'd stand right over you.
Where was this at? That's in Smithfield. In where? Smithfield. Is that nearby? I want to tell you from Baton Rouge. Oh yeah.
It's across the river from Baton Rouge, twelve miles north.
North of Port Allen? Yeah. I think I know where it is.
I used to go to different places. I'm at the Wildwood.
He know them. He know them. Yes.

And you always, you cut cane out there? Yes, yes. Well you were a grown man then, huh? Oh yes. You couldn't keep up, you couldn't keep up with me. I'm a grown man. I'm a grown man. I'm a grown man. I'm a grown man. You couldn't keep up though, huh? Well I could keep up.
I'd keep fast up. I'd get way up in there so the man wouldn't follow me. That's the reason I didn't cut it good all the time.
Well you just, he wanted you to tighten up, huh?
When I tightened up, I wasn't half cut it. Yeah. Well then, I'll get up in there and cut it right. Mm-hmm. I see.
